hook: SCP-1471 is short and very modern: a free phone app that quietly installs itself into someone's life. Reading it on your own phone adds to the effect. The unease builds through steady accumulation rather than one big scare.
whyItMatters: The entry takes the cursed-media idea and moves it into an app store listing, with download size, version number and a sales pitch. The tags pair 'uncontained' with a file that reports no hostile acts, an odd combination that keeps you unsure whether this is a haunting or a strange form of company.
thingsToNotice:
The timeline is the engine: in the first day the photos show places the owner often goes, by 48 hours places they visited recently, and by 72 hours live shots of the owner with the canine-skulled figure right beside them. Past roughly 90 hours the figure starts showing up in the corner of the eye and in reflections, and beyond that it never goes away; cutting off the images before then is the only known fix.

The store listing at the end recasts everything. It is dedicated to a redacted name, has zero reviews, and sells the app as a cure for loneliness that draws closer the more you engage, so the figure reads as a companion being marketed. Combined with the note that no harm has been recorded, the creature's failed attempts to communicate are what linger, and the caption on the opening image hints at just how many phones the Foundation has already seized.
